title: The Dear friend from school
subtitle: 友谊关系 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 友谊关系（社会服务与人际沟通·友谊与人际关系）
meta: 主题语境：友谊关系（社会服务与人际沟通·友谊与人际关系）　|　核心词汇：dear　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dear 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1990 the gardener wrote of ① a dear friend from school in the notebook, and everybody in the garden said at once that it was ② dearer than the one named there the year before. Three springs on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the gardener, who never explained anything, had done it year after year and gone home; it was the dear ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the dearest friend from school anybody in the garden had ever seen, or so the notebook for April 1984 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too dear to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the apprentice who had come to help; the dear ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the trowel at the far bed, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a dear price for the wool, and said that no apprentice in his right mind would call it ⑥ as dear as the price for the wool they had once had in the old garden. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was dear or not, and he said so.

By 1997 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the notebook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something dear, and nothing besides. The apprentice from the next garden called the whole plan ⑧ quite dear; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the notebook kept the names of the dear ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 2000, for the whole place, she wrote of another dear friend from school in the same notebook, and the work, which took two springs, seemed ⑨ dearer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The dearest price for the wool in the whole garden, she said in 2002, was the one she could never quite name; the dear ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 亲爱（前置定语 a dear friend from school：1990 年园丁在园艺笔记里记下的那件亲爱的挚友）
B. adj. 亲爱／昂贵（比较级 dearer than：文中两处，一处比上学时的挚友，一处比预想）
C. adj. 亲爱／昂贵（最高级 the dearest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 亲爱（表语 too dear to do：母亲觉得它太亲爱，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 昂贵（前置定语 a dear price for the wool：叔叔把整件事称作一桩昂贵的价钱）
F. adj. 昂贵（同级比较 as dear as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩羊毛的价钱相比）
G. adj. 昂贵（后置定语 something dear：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 昂贵（受程度副词修饰 quite dear：那位学徒的评价）

items.q: the dearest friend from school anybody
a dear price for the wool
The dearest price for the wool in

answers.why: dear 意为“亲爱”，1990 年园丁在园艺笔记里记下的是“一件亲爱的挚友”，此处作前置定语 a dear friend from school。
dear 意为“亲爱”，此处用比较级 dearer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
dear 意为“亲爱”，园艺笔记上 四月 那行字说它是园子里最亲爱的一件，故用最高级 the dearest friend from school。
dear 意为“亲爱”，母亲认为这件东西“太亲爱了，谁也用不上”，too dear to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
dear 意为“昂贵”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩昂贵的价钱”，此处作前置定语 a dear price for the wool。
dear 意为“昂贵”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩羊毛的价钱一样昂贵”，同级比较用 as dear as。
dear 意为“昂贵”，园艺笔记上那半行字要的是“昂贵的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something dear。
dear 意为“昂贵”，邻园子来的那位学徒认为这套计划“相当昂贵”，quite 修饰原级 dear。
dear 意为“昂贵”，2000 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要昂贵”，故用比较级 dearer than。
dear 意为“昂贵”，母亲 2002 年说的是“整个园子里最昂贵的那一桩”，故用最高级 the dearest price for the wool。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1990 年，园丁在园艺笔记里记下了一件亲爱的挚友。（a dear friend from school）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更亲爱。（dearer than …）
母亲觉得它太亲爱，谁也用不上。（too dear to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩昂贵的价钱。（a dear price for the wool）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩羊毛的价钱一样昂贵。（as dear as …）
到了 1997 年，园艺笔记上只剩半行字：要的是一件昂贵的东西。（something dear）
answers: In 1990 the gardener wrote of a dear friend from school in the notebook.
Everybody said it was dearer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too dear to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a dear price for the wool.
He said nobody would call it as dear as the price for the wool they had once had.
By 1997 the notebook asked for nothing but something dear.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 dear 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1990 the gardener wrote of a dear friend from school in the notebook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the dearest friend from school in the garden, or so the notebook says.
My mother thought it too dear to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a dear price for the wool, and nobody argued with him.
The apprentice from the next garden called the plan quite dear, and everybody laughed.
The dear ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
